origin.description: Accessory outline, phone-facing. XY origin is the magnet-ring center (Pixelsnap axis). +X is phone right, +Y is toward the camera bar (phone top), +Z is out of the phone (away from glass).

phone.notes: Pixel 10 published body 152.8 x 72.0 x 8.6 mm (GSMArena / Google). Camera-bar length and Pixelsnap center are published defaults. Replace them after you caliper a real unit. Do not invent caliper numbers.

magnet.vendor: totalElement R54X46X15MMN52-5PK. The 54.1 x 46 x 1.5 mm N52 ring already has its steel plate glued on. The alignment magnet is the separate 12 x 5 mm block in that pack. Its long side points at 6 o'clock (phone bottom, -Y), centered on the ring, so the case cannot spin. Blind wells, 0.85 mm non-ferrous skin toward the phone. Glue the steel face. Do not put tape in the magnetic gap, and do not add a second steel disc.

accessory.size_note: Compact-final spin: 62 x 88 x 10.65 mm. Speaker is gone. Dev / USB-C variant (branch revert-to-usb-c): J2 is a mid-mount USB-C on the phone-bottom edge; the magnetic pad is gone. The 59.6 x 85.6 board fills the case to one 1.2 mm wall per side. Lid is always natural translucent PETG so D1 and D2 read through it. Tray is PETG first, then 6061. The phone face is closed: 0.85 mm skin, then blind wells for the 1.5 mm N52 ring and the clocking magnet. Four M1.6 posts. The 3.3 mm Jauch pouch is taped to the board underside. Tray is 6.85 mm and the lid is 3.80 mm. The extra 0.10 mm over the old 10.55 mm shell is the DigiKey pack's 3.3 mm max vs the previous 3.2 mm cell.

pcb.usb_diff_note: Not impedance controlled, on purpose. The ESP32-S3 USB-OTG peripheral is full speed only (12 Mbps, no high-speed PHY: Espressif's USB overview table marks ESP32-S3 'USB OTG High-Speed = X'). F.Cu sits 0.1 mm above the In1 GND plane in this stackup, where a 90 ohm differential pair would need roughly 0.06 mm traces, well under the 0.127 mm any quick-turn fab will run. Rather than thicken the prepreg for a requirement the silicon does not have, D+/D- run as a 0.2 mm pair on a 0.4 mm pitch over solid In1 GND, which is near 75 ohm differential by first-order microstrip. The run is long for a USB pair because U1's USB pads are on the module's top row, the far side of a 15.9 mm module from the connector, and its castellations leave 0.05 mm between pads so nothing crosses the footprint. At full-speed edge rates it is still electrically short. Measured copper is in hardware/kicad/recorder/placement.json under routing.usb, written by route_pcb.py from the board itself. Do not re-type those millimetres into this sentence: this note and the one in placement.json each carried their own hand-typed lengths and both went stale at the first reroute.

connectors.pogo_note: J2 is Xinyangze YZ103915020T-04025-02 (LCSC C6276862) at (0, 36), the phone-top / camera end, opposite the 6 o'clock clocking magnet in the tray. Vendor drawing and LCSC EasyEDA land: 22.30 x 7.70 x 2.00 mm stadium (full-radius ends), 4 pins at 2.54 mm. The lid dishes down over the pad so the gold is 0.15 mm proud of that local face. The rest of the lid stays tall for the 2.4 mm MCU. Cable male is YZP0048-20048-04025-03 (C5126845). Footprint rot 0, so pin 1 VBUS is on the phone-left side of the pad. Pin order is 1 VBUS, 2 USB_DM, 3 USB_DP, 4 GND until a click-test says otherwise. No USB-C and no wall mouth.
connectors.pogo_obsolete_note: OBSOLETE on this branch (revert-to-usb-c, dev / USB-C variant). J2 is no longer the magnetic pad, so every pogo_* key above describes a part that is not on the board. Kept only until the case agent removes the pogo dish / well from case.scad. Use the usbc_* keys. check_placement.py reads usbc_x_mm / usbc_y_mm, not pogo_x_mm / pogo_y_mm.
connectors.usbc_part: HRO TYPE-C-31-M-13C, LCSC C2848620, 16-pin USB 2.0 Type-C receptacle, mid-mount (sink board)
connectors.usbc_edge_note: Phone-bottom short edge (-Y, the board edge at y = -42.8), mouth pointing -Y. usbc_x_mm / usbc_y_mm are the KiCad footprint origin (twin of placement.json J2); the mouth centre line is x = usbc_x_mm. It is 7.0 mm phone-right of the magnet axis, not centred, because the BQ24073 / LDO / load-switch row owns the rest of that edge.
connectors.usbc_front_note: Shell front face is flush with the board edge (HRO drawing: 2.10 mm from the PCB edge to the front shell legs; LCSC 3D model ends on the slot mouth). Positive would mean proud of the board edge. The 0.3 mm pcb_clear rebate plus the wall sit in front of it, so the plug crosses about 1.2 mm of case before it meets the shell.
connectors.usbc_height_note: Heights are from the HRO drawing, measured from the board top surface (F.Cu). Shell top is 1.60 above F.Cu; total shell height is 3.16, so the shell bottom is 1.56 below F.Cu, i.e. 0.76 below B.Cu on this 0.8 mm board. Mouth centre is 0.02 above F.Cu (usbc_mouth_z_mm). With the board top at z = 6.85 mm (tray_h), the shell spans z = 5.29 .. 8.45 above the phone face and the mouth centre is at z = 6.87, right on the tray / lid seam. The lid cavity ceiling is 9.45, so 1.0 mm over the shell. Under the board, the shell and its four legs sit in the slot / outside the pouch (pouch ends at y = -33.0), above the 2.35 mm tray floor.
connectors.usbc_slot_note: Board cutout (Edge.Cuts, carried in the J2 footprint): 9.24 mm wide, 6.54 mm deep, open on the y = -42.8 edge. Mill corners will round to the router radius (about 0.5 mm) at the two back corners. Nothing in the tray may rise into this rectangle above z = 5.2.
connectors.usbc_plug_note: USB-IF maximum plug overmold is 12.35 x 6.5 mm. Centred on the mouth (z = 6.87) it spans z = 3.62 .. 10.12: 3.6 mm clear of the phone back and 0.53 mm under the 10.65 mm lid top, so it hits neither. The overmold will butt the outside of the case wall. A Type-C plug needs the overmold within roughly 0.5-1 mm of the receptacle face to latch fully, so give the wall an overmold relief (about 12.8 x 7.0 mm, local wall thinned to <= 0.5 mm, or an open pocket) around a shell clearance mouth of about 9.5 x 3.7 mm. The relief straddles the tray / lid seam.
connectors.mic_note: MK1 (IM73A135, bottom port) goes at (27.5, 17.0) rot 90 on F.Cu, which puts its 0.8 mm NPTH at (27.5, 16.32) on B.Cu. Phone-right wall. The tray rib stops 0.40 mm short of the board for a foam frame, with a mesh pocket under that and three 0.60 mm wall holes at 1.10 mm pitch. The port stays off the steel shunt (r = 28.5). check_envelope holds these to placement.json.
connectors.button_note: SW1 (EVQP7C01P, rot 270) puts its actuator tip button_tip_inset_mm inside the phone-left board edge: x = -29.2 at this outline, so SW1 centre is x = -27.1. That is the left wall when the accessory is snapped on the phone. The actuator face is 1.7 mm wide and 0.3-1.2 mm above the board (button_actuator_z_mm is its centre, from the KiCad 3D model). The finger target is a captive TPU 95A pill in the lid: a rounded-rect bezel flush with the wall and a smaller rounded press pad that stands proud, like an iPhone-case side button. SW1 is the spring.
connectors.batt_pad_note: BT1 is two solder pads for the pouch pigtail on B.Cu at (-17, 35), west of J2 and just north of the cell (ends at y = 33). Rot 0 puts pad 1 VBAT on the west land. The 66 mm pack is still centred at (0, 0); J2's courtyard fills the centreline under the pad, so the joints sit in the aisle west of the magnetic pad. Tape the cell on and kapton the joints. Twin to placement.json BT1.

battery.offset_note: Jauch LP305166JH pack taped to the board underside at (0, 0), then wrapped in kapton including the face toward the shunt. DigiKey envelope is 66 x 51.5 x 3.3 mm; the 70 mm leads solder to B.Cu BT1 at (-17, 35). The four M1.6 posts carry the board. About 0.15 mm of air under the wrapped cell so the pouch is not a spacer. F.Cu under the pouch outline is free.
battery.chemistry: Jauch LP305166JH 1S1P LiPo with PCM and 70 mm leads, DigiKey 13278052. Nominal 3.7 V, charge 4.2 V, min 1200 mAh / typ 1220 mAh. Pack envelope 66.0 x 51.5 x 3.3 mm (the Jauch cell catalogue line is 3.0 x 51.0 x 68.0 mm). PCM on the pack; this board still has no second protector. Charge at 500 mA is under the pack's 0.5 C / 600 mA ceiling.

mounting.note: Screws from the PETG lid (clearance + outer CSK) into M1.6 tapped in four 5.0 mm tray posts. The tap drill is 1.35 mm, 2.5 mm deep, and stops above the 2.35 mm inner floor. The 0.85 mm phone-face skin stays closed. Do not print threads.

antenna.note: Lid-only radio. Buy Inventek B24P-W (DigiKey 1475-B24P-W-ND): 2.4 GHz 50 ohm adhesive 30 x 5 x 0.5 mm polymer patch, W.FL / I-PEX MHF III plug, 102 mm 0.81 mm coax. That jack mates the MINI-1U third-gen connector (Espressif: W.FL / MHF III / Amphenol AMC). Do not buy a first-generation U.FL plug. IPEX local XY is footprint-local on U1 (connector toward +X/+Y at rot 0). World XY is U1 at (14, -18) rot 0. 7.0 mm well, 0.85 mm into the 1.2 mm PETG skin, leaves 0.35 mm. Do not enlarge that well. Tape mark is 30 x 5 mm at (-2, -33), long axis along +X, phone-bottom end, clear of J2, SW1, and the four bosses. Straight-line to the well is about 28 mm; coil the extra 102 mm slack in the 2.60 mm lid cavity. Mate the pigtail only when sharing.
